FREIGHT FORWARDER TERMINAL AREAS:
Freight forwarders assemble and consolidate shipments and provide break-bulk and delivery services for the shipping public. The forwarders hold themselves out to provide, in their own name and under their own responsibility, a through transportation service from the point of receipt of a shipment to final destination. Significantly, however, forwarders 47 are required by statute to rely on the use of other common carriers for the performance of the transportation services they provide, with the exception of "the performance within terminal areas of transfer, collection, or delivery services."

Thus, forwarders must contract with carriers subject to Parts I (rail), II (motor), and III (water) of the Act to provide the actual transportation of their traffic, although they are
^{46}
A freight forwarder is defined in section 402(a)(5) of the Act, 49 U.S.C. 1002(a)(5) (1970), as:
***
any person which (otherwise than as a carrier subject to part I, II, or III of this Act) holds itself out to the general public as a common carrier to transport or provide transportation of property, or any class or classes of property, for compensation, in interstate commerce, and which, in the ordinary and usual course of its undertaking, (A) assembles and consolidates or provides for assembling and consolidating shipments of such property, and performs or provides for the performance of break-bulk and distributing operations with respect to such consolidated shipments, and (B) assumes responsibility for the transportation of such property from point of receipt to point of destination, and (C) utilizes, for the whole or any part of the transportation of such shipments, the services of a carrier or carriers subject to part I, II, or III of this Act.
&
lt;sup>47</sup>Section 418 of the Interstate Commerce Act, 49 U.S.C. 1018 (1970).
&
lt;sup>48</sup>Within terminal areas, forwarders may provide their own pickup and delivery service utilizing their own equipment. Alternatively, forwarders may hire unregulated motor carriers to perform such service. Common carrier authority is not required for a terminal area operation, since it is regulated as an element of the general forwarder operation.
